paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity.
model_annotation: This figure is a nested donut chart (also called a concentric pie chart) that displays the distribution of samples across two related ambiguity metrics. The outer ring represents the Ambiguity Standard Deviation (Std) with four slices: Std: 0.0 in very dark navy/teal at 49.0%, Std: 0.47 in dark blue at 47.7%, Std: 0.82 in medium dark teal at 7.0%, and Std: 0.94 in medium blue at 5.0%. The inner ring represents the Max Ambiguity with three slices: Max: 1 in a medium cyan/sky blue at 38.0%, Max: 2 in a lighter cyan blue at 39.0%, and Max: 3 in a very light cyan/ice blue at 14.2%. The outer ring appears to be dominated by two large slices (Std: 0.0 and Std: 0.47), which together account for approximately 96.7% of the distribution, while the remaining two slices are relatively small. In the inner ring, the Max: 1 and Max: 2 categories are roughly equal in size, with Max: 3 being notably smaller. Percentage labels are displayed on or near each slice. Two separate legends are positioned to the right of the chart, one for the outer ring labeled 'Ambiguity Std (Outer)' and one for the inner ring labeled 'Max Ambiguity (Inner)', each showing the category labels with their corresponding colors.
